meta.title: Oil
meta.description: Upstream, exports, refining and oil-price trends through the year 1404. The data is sample and unreal.

articles.title: Redevelopment contract signed for a mature southern oil field
articles.lead: In this sample, a contract has been signed to raise output from an old onshore field, aiming to add 85,000 barrels per day over four years.
body: On this item's invented account, the project is worth 1.9 billion hypothetical currency units and covers 40 new wells, renewal of gathering pipelines and a new desalting unit.

In the same scenario, the field's recovery factor rises from 24 to 31 percent through gas injection and reservoir-pressure management. The first noticeable output gain is expected 18 months after operations start.
This text reports no real event; every figure, body and timeframe was built to show the oil service page.
articles.author: Business Desk

articles.title: Crude and condensate exports rose in spring 1404
articles.lead: On this sample's invented data, first-quarter exports averaged 1.65 million barrels per day, about 7 percent above winter.
body: On this report's hypothetical figures, East Asia was the top destination with a 68 percent share, and gas condensate made up about a fifth of all cargoes.
In the same scenario, floating storage near export terminals fell to its lowest in 18 months, read in this sample as a sign of smoother deliveries.
This story is fabricated and made to test how export data displays in the oil service; none of its numbers rests on a real source.
articles.author: Business Desk

articles.title: Refinery upgrade lifts gasoline output and cuts sulphur
articles.lead: In this sample, a refinery's new treatment unit added 12 million litres a day of Euro-5 gasoline capacity.
body: On this item's invented text, the project includes a catalytic reforming unit and a desulphurisation unit, with investment stated at 950 million hypothetical currency units.
In the same scenario, average sulphur in the output gasoline fell from 50 to under 10 ppm, and the refinery's fuel-oil yield dropped about 15 percent.
Every figure and technical spec in this text is hypothetical and written only to show how refining news is covered in this demo.
articles.author: Energy Desk

articles.title: Sample analysis: Brent holds a narrow range into late summer
articles.lead: In this hypothetical note, the Demo Analysis Desk expects Brent to swing between 78 and 85 fictional units.
body: On this analysis's invented assumptions, seasonal refinery demand and steady supply are the two balancing forces, and a break of the range is likely only with a supply shock.
In the same text, the quality spread between the heavy and light baskets has widened slightly, which the hypothetical author reads as refiners favouring lighter feed this season.
This note is not investment advice, has no real data, and exists only to show the market-analysis format in this demo's oil service.
articles.author: Business Desk

articles.title: Enhanced-recovery pilot reports a higher recovery factor
articles.lead: In this sample, smart water injection in a test block raised the recovery factor by 4 percentage points in two years.
body: On this report's invented figures, the test block used six producing wells and three injectors, with the salinity of the injected water tuned to disrupt oil sticking to rock.
In the same scenario, the operator says that extending the method to the whole field would add about 90 million barrels of cumulative output over a decade.
This text is not sourced; all its technical and economic detail was built to show the upstream news structure.
articles.author: Field Reporting

articles.title: New floating storage adds flexibility at the export terminal
articles.lead: In this sample, a 2-million-barrel storage vessel has been added to the main export terminal to better manage loading schedules.
body: On this item's hypothetical text, the new vessel lets loading continue on high-swell days without a full stop, cutting tanker waiting time by about 11 hours.
In the same scenario, the operator says this back-up capacity trims ship-demurrage costs by roughly 7 million hypothetical currency units a year.
This story is fabricated and written only to complete the export news list in this demo's oil service.
articles.author: Business Desk

articles.title: Sample report: refining margins narrow as product supply improves
articles.lead: In this sample, a hypothetical regional refining-margin index is down about 18 percent from the previous month.
body: On this report's invented figures, several refining units returning from maintenance, plus higher gasoline and diesel stocks, have put downward pressure on margins.
In the same hypothetical text, part of the drop is expected to reverse as the cold season nears and heating-gasoil demand grows.
This piece has no sourced data and was built only to show the market-report format in the oil service.
articles.author: Business Desk

articles.title: Heavy-crude discount widens on a bigger quality spread
articles.lead: In this sample, the price gap between heavy crude and the light basket has reached 6.5 fictional units per barrel.
body: On this analysis's invented assumptions, limited conversion-unit capacity at some regional refineries has softened demand for heavy feed and deepened its discount.
In the same scenario, if several new coking units start up on schedule, the discount is expected to narrow somewhat in later quarters.
This note is not trading advice, and all its numbers were built to show the price-analysis structure in this demo.
